text.p: SKOPJE, Nov 5 (Retuer) - These are the leading stories in hte Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Greek constructors say they are interested in reconstrucion of the Macedonian hydroelectric power stations and border crossings.

- There have been no incidents at the Greek-Macedonian border since the Interim Accord between the two countries was signed a year ago. Only few attempts of illegal border crossings have been registered.
- Turkish and Macedonian businessmen said economic cooperation between the two countries went far beyond friendly political relations. Bilateral trade stood at $93.5 million in 1995.
- Japan secured five million dollars in aid for Macedonian health institutions.
- The council of Europe, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe and the U.S. National Democratic Institute to send observers for the republic's November 17 elections.
- Only 37 small agricultural and industrial enterprises used foreign credits worth 2.5 million German marks. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom, ++389 91 201 196
